title: Grothendieck abelian categories are locally presentable
statement: Let $\mathcal B$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with small Hom sets in a fixed universe $\mathcal U$, and take small colimits relative to $\mathcal U$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $\mathcal B$ is locally presentable: for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$ in $\mathcal U$ there is a $\mathcal U$-small set of objects $\mathcal G$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(G,-)$ preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits for every $G\in\mathcal G$, and every object is a $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects of $\mathcal G$. Here an indexing category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram in it with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone. An infinite cardinal is regular if a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets, each of cardinality less than $\kappa$, still has cardinality less than $\kappa$.
